A.explanation: Doppler shift is caused by relative motion between source and observer and so occurs for all wave motions, including sound, water and light.

B.explanation: It is true for light and sound, but it is not limited to them since a moving source in a ripple tank also shows a Doppler shift in water waves.

C.explanation: It is true for sound and water waves, but it also occurs for light, as seen in the red shift of light from receding galaxies.

D.explanation: Sound is only the most familiar example, such as a passing siren, but the same wavefront crowding and spreading applies to other waves.

hints: Notice the wording asks for which types of wave in general, not just the familiar ambulance siren example for sound.
Connect the Doppler shift to its cause - relative motion along the line joining source and observer changing the observed wavelength $\lambda$ and frequency $f$.
Compare the three named examples - sound waves, water ripples and light - and ask whether a moving source crowds wavefronts ahead of it in each case.
walkthrough: Identify what the question tests: whether the Doppler change in observed frequency and wavelength depends on the medium or type of wave.

State the governing physics: when there is relative motion of source and observer, successive wavefronts are emitted from different positions, so the observed wavelength $\lambda_o$ is changed and hence the observed frequency $f_o$ is changed.

Apply this cause-and-effect chain to mechanical waves: a moving sound source gives a higher pitch on approach and lower pitch on recession, and a moving dipper in a ripple tank gives shorter water wavelengths ahead and longer wavelengths behind.

Apply the same chain to electromagnetic waves: relative motion changes the observed wavelength of light, observed as blue shift on approach and red shift on recession, even though no medium is required.
Since sound, water and light all show the effect, there is no restriction to one family of waves. This is option A.
